lede: A GPU-first FDTD electromagnetic solver written in Rust. It simulates in 3-D, 2-D or 2.5-D, takes gdsfactory layouts to S-parameters and inverse-design gradients, and runs on one GPU, several GPUs or several machines.

quickstart.title: Quick start
quickstart.code:
import gdsfactory as gf, numpy as np
from lightsim.sparams import write_sparameters

gf.gpdk.PDK.activate()
sp = write_sparameters(
    gf.components.mmi1x2(),
    wavelengths=np.linspace(1.5e-6, 1.6e-6, 21),
    device="cuda:0",
)
print(abs(sp["o2@0,o1@0"]) ** 2)   # 0.49 at 1.55 um
quickstart.caption: A gdsfactory component goes in; the port modes are solved on the simulation grid and the S-parameters come back: about 42 s on one RTX PRO 6000 at the default resolution, 28 s with port symmetry.
